_comment: The key set an issuer publishes at /v1/keyset, as an operator configures it and as it is served. Keys are listed in the order they became active; the first is the anchor; each later key carries introduced_by, the composite signature of the key before it over the canonical JSON of {ctx: 'aria-keyset-introduction-v1', key_id, suite, public_key_mldsa65, public_key_ed25519, active_from, previous}, where previous is the entry before it in full (key_id, suite, both keys, active_from, active_until); only the last key is active (active_until null). anchor is the fingerprint of the first key, configured apart from the set: a set whose first key is not the anchor is refused, and so is any set that rewrites an accepted entry, since the introduction after it no longer verifies. fingerprint is 'sha256:' and the hex SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of {key_id, suite, public_key_mldsa65, public_key_ed25519}. A verifier trusts the key whose fingerprint it pinned out of band; publication grants nothing. The gateway serving these test keys verifies with the active key. Synthetic keys derived from public labels.

refused.label: the first key carries an introduction
a later key without an introduction
an introduction by the key itself
an introduction signed over another start
the introduced key replaced after signing
a suite other than the composite one
a member the format does not define
the active key is not the one the gateway verifies with
an active window that ends before it starts
the history truncated: the first key dropped, the next made the anchor
the anchor replaced by another key that introduces the same successor
an accepted entry rewritten: the anchor retired later than recorded
an accepted entry rewritten: the anchor active earlier than recorded
a key fragment outside the published alphabet
